questions.question_text: An account pays $7\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly and is held for $6$ years. Which pair gives the rate per period and the number of periods?

options.why: Counted the quarters but left the rate as the annual rate instead of dividing by $4$.
Divided the rate by $4$ but left $n$ as the number of years.
Used $2$ periods a year, the half-yearly divisor, instead of $4$ for quarterly.

questions.question_text: An account pays $8.4\%$ p.a. compounded monthly and is held for $5$ years. Which pair gives the rate per period and the number of periods?

options.why: Counted the months but left the rate as the annual rate instead of dividing by $12$.
Divided the rate by $12$ but left $n$ as the number of years.
Used $4$ periods a year, the quarterly divisor, instead of $12$ for monthly.

questions.question_text: $\$9\,000$ is placed in an account paying $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly for $5$ years. Find the balance, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Compounded once a year at $4.8\%$, ignoring the quarterly compounding.
Divided the rate by $4$ but used $n=5$ years instead of $20$ quarters.
Used $20$ quarters with the full annual rate of $4.8\%$ per quarter.

questions.question_text: $\$1\,800$ is placed in an account paying $3.6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly for $3$ years. Find the balance, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Compounded once a year at $3.6\%$, ignoring the monthly compounding.
Divided the rate by $12$ but used $n=3$ years instead of $36$ months.
Used $36$ months with the full annual rate of $3.6\%$ per month.

questions.question_text: $\$25\,000$ is invested in a bond paying $6\%$ p.a. compounded half-yearly for $7$ years. Find the **interest earned**, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Gave the balance without subtracting the $\$25\,000$ invested.
Compounded once a year at $6\%$, ignoring the half-yearly compounding.
Halved the rate but used $n=7$ years instead of $14$ half-years.

questions.question_text: An account pays $5.2\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly. How much must be deposited now for the balance to be $\$12\,000$ in $6$ years? Answer to the nearest cent.

options.why: Compounded once a year at $5.2\%$, ignoring the quarterly compounding.
Divided the rate by $4$ but used $n=6$ years instead of $24$ quarters.
Multiplied by $(1.013)^{24}$ instead of dividing, growing the balance again.

questions.question_text: $\$4\,000$ is placed in an account paying $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly for $2.5$ years. Find the balance, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Left the rate annual and used $n=2.5$ instead of matching both to months.
Rounded the term down to $2$ years, using $n=24$ instead of $30$ months.
Gave the interest earned rather than the balance in the account.

questions.question_text: $\$10\,000$ is invested for $3$ years at $4.8\%$ p.a. How much more is the balance when the account compounds monthly rather than quarterly? Answer to the nearest cent.

options.why: Compared monthly compounding with yearly compounding instead of with quarterly.
Compared quarterly compounding with yearly compounding instead of the two given options.
Gave the monthly balance instead of the difference between the two balances.

questions.question_text: A superannuation account is projected to be worth $\$480\,000$ in $25$ years at $5\%$ p.a. compounded half-yearly. What single amount invested now would produce the same future value? Answer to the nearest dollar.

options.why: Compounded once a year at $5\%$, ignoring the half-yearly compounding.
Halved the rate but used $n=25$ years instead of $50$ half-years.
Multiplied by $(1.025)^{50}$ instead of dividing, projecting forward again.
